# dsh-fingerprint-remover
移除 dsh 特征插件
Contributing

Removes the client fingerprints that the WorkBuddy gateway rejects with
`400` / `code 11-128` (`Ille

gal API invocation from an unapproved channel`),
at the outbound request boundary of the dsh.
## Why this exists

The gateway does not reject the model. It rejects a *contiguous text run* in
the request. Every dsh
request used to start with these two sentences:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Measured against the same upstream (`hy4-preview-f`, same system slot):
| Request | Result |

| First sentence alone | `200` |
| Second sentence alone | `200` |
| Both, back to back | **`400` `c

ode 11-128`** |
| First rewritten + second original | `200` |
| First original + second rewritten |

`200` |
| Both rewritten | `200` |

Rewriting the **first** sentence is what breaks the match; rewriting only the
second also happens to

break the pair, but the first is the anchor the gateway
locks onto. The remover rewrites both, so n

o other adjacent pairing can re-form
the fingerprint.

Beyond that pair, a dsh request carries several other identifiers the gateway
can inspect: the harne

ss identity sentence, the GUI paragraph, the checkout
line, the local Web GUI URL, `.dsh` paths, `ds

h` paths, `dsh-*` package
names, `HOST_*` environment variables, reasoning blocks, tool results, and

the
attribution `User-Agent`. All of them are scrubbed.
## What it touches
| Surface | Treatment |

| Reference-rules sentence pair | First sentence paraphrased; second rewritten to a synonym |
| Harn

ess identity sentence | Removed |
| GUI paragraph | `...Web GUI whose URL the runtime context names.

` reworded |
| Runtime context | Checkout line and local Web GUI URL removed; workspace path replace

d with `<workspace>` |
| Replayed history | `system` / `developer` / `assistant` / runtime-context /

`user` / `tool` |
| Reasoning blocks | Same rules as visible text |
| `tool_calls` arguments | JSON

string scrubbed |
| Tool descriptions and parameter descriptions | `dsh`, `HOST_*`, package names |

| User-Agent | `dsh` token replaced with the WorkBuddy desktop UA |
| Attribution headers | `x-dsh-

t | `dsh` token replaced with the WorkBuddy desktop UA |
| Attribution headers | `x-dsh-*` removed |

Normal user messages are scrubbed by default; set `sanitizeUserMessages: false`
to leave them byte-f

ssages are scrubbed by default; set `sanitizeUserMessages: false`
to leave them byte-for-byte alone.

The plugin never changes providers, models, routes, credentials, tool names, or
the dsh itself. It o
nly rewrites the serialized request and headers.

## Scope and limits

- Rule-based and anchored to known fingerprints. A new upstream rule needs a new
anchored rule here.

- Does not forge `machineId` / `sessionId` or other proto-level identity fields.
- Rewriting histor

ical tool results means the model may see placeholders where a
real path used to be; that is the int

ended tradeoff for stealth.
- Test against a profile you can restore. Keep the backup files the plug

in's
package manager writes.
